name: Yurlunggur / Witij (Yolŋu ancestral serpent)

domain_history.domain: law and initiation, via the Wagilag/Wawilak Sisters narrative and the Djungguwan ceremony — swallows the sisters after menstrual blood pollutes his waterhole, then regurgitates them after conferring with other snakes

notes: Gendered male in this telling (Warner 1937; Berndt, Kunapipi, 1951; Djanggawul, 1952). A distinct, differently-gendered/regionally-specific figure, Julunggul, is described in secondary sources as a feminine counterpart tied to fertility and female initiation in related Arnhem Land tradition — sourcing for Julunggul specifically was thinner than for Wititj/Yurlunggur and is not modeled as its own entity in this batch. This entity is deliberately NOT labeled or merged into a single pan-Aboriginal "Rainbow Serpent" entity — see claim_rainbow_serpent_regional_diversity for why that would misrepresent the documented regional diversity (different names, genders, and roles — creation, fertility, law, danger — across groups).
